solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He's in a tragic play, primarily? Could be?

definitions.text: He's in a tragic play, primarily? Could be?

indicators.note: the question 'could be?' invites the letters to be arranged some other way

parts.note: the apostrophe gives no letter, so this is just H, E, S
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether someone appears in a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' signals the anagram of HE'S IN A plus T and P, the first letters of 'tragic play' picked out by 'primarily'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is someone who appears in plays, tragic ones included.

clue.text: Wealthy sort's home to measure carpet

indicators.note: being home to something means holding it inside

parts.note: a toff is British slang for a rich, upper-class person
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A rich person's house where someone measures up for a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' looks like a floor covering but is a verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British usage for reprimanding them, as if called onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Put away starter of lamb perhaps?

indicators.note: the starter of the word is dropped, leaving the rest

parts.note: lamb is one example of meat

explanation.surface: Finishing off a lamb starter at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To put food away is informal for consuming it, often in quantity.

clue.text: God, he exists in the heart of matter? Yes, ultimately — so they believe

definitions.text: God, he exists in the heart of matter? Yes, ultimately — so they believe

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the following letters
the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle pair

parts.note: taken as written
is means exists, as in 'there is'

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A believer's statement that God lives at the core of all matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' takes the middle pair of letters of 'matter', which hold the next two words; 'ultimately' adds the end of 'Yes'. The whole clue is also a summary of the belief.
explanation.definitionFit: People holding that the divine is identical with the universe and everything in it believe exactly this.

clue.text: Copper ignored minister's crime

indicators.note: ignored means that letter is left out

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church
P stands for penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A policeman overlooked a clergyman's offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer; it is a copper coin, a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: Lackey regularly returns bearing a cake

indicators.note: returns means the picked letters are read backwards
regularly takes every other letter of the word Lackey, starting with the first

parts.note: a person's bearing is their air or manner

explanation.surface: A servant comes back carrying a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger filled with cream and iced on top is a classic cake.

clue.text: It helps preserve wine and port

definitions.meaning: a bottle stopper keeping air out
a harbour city in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: Something that keeps both table wine and port fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: The bark stopper seals a bottle; it is also a seaport city in southern Ireland.

clue.text: Touring US city turned one old man to drink

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the city
turned means the letters are twisted into a different order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, and the other three words are taken as written
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An old man on a tour of an American city takes to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' shuffles I (one) with the letters of 'old man to' into AMONTILDO, and 'Touring' sets the city inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-dry Spanish sherry is a fortified wine, so a drink.

clue.text: Peacekeepers must stop rising hostilities ever getting out of control

indicators.note: stop as in plug a gap, so these letters go inside the next piece
in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: war is open hostilities
UN peacekeeping forces, the United Nations
ay is an old word meaning always

explanation.surface: Blue helmets must step in before fighting spirals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the hostilities upwards, giving RAW, before the peacekeepers go in; AY is an archaic word for ever, and 'getting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway train or inflation is one no longer under control.

clue.text: Scholar's better organised — he could have you for breakfast!

definitions.text: he could have you for breakfast!

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree
neater means tidier, better arranged

explanation.surface: A tidy academic boasts that he could eat you alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater, a tiger or a predatory lover, devours people; the exclamation is a playful hint.

clue.text: Abandon reserve and be a disappointment to shock?

definitions.meaning: to relax and stop being inhibited, as at a party
read literally: a shock of hair is let down, i.e. disappointed

explanation.walkthrough: A 'shock' is also a thick mass of hair, and to 'let down' is to disappoint, so the second reading is a joke about failing one's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to relax and enjoy oneself; read word by word it means failing a mop of hair, a shock.

clue.text: Depend on a husband disposed to be generous

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Relying on a husband who happens to be generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed to be generous' reads as one phrase, but 'disposed' is the anagram signal and 'to be' just joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an open palm gives freely, so the hyphenated adjective means liberal or giving.

clue.text: Remaining houses to demolish finally abandoned — that's wasteful

indicators.note: houses as a verb means holds inside

parts.note: extant means still in existence

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to ravage is to wreck or destroy

explanation.surface: The remaining houses due for demolition are finally abandoned, which is a waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like buildings but is a verb; 'finally abandoned' strips the last letter from the synonym for demolish, giving RAVAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending lavishly or without restraint is the very opposite of thrift.

clue.text: Fix wimp's wheels

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a wimp is a wet in British slang; with 's this gives WETS

explanation.surface: Repairing the wheels belonging to a feeble person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a noun belonging to the wimp; it is a verb, turning the letters round. A 'wet' is British slang for a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fix and being in a stew both mean being in a state of trouble or agitation.

clue.text: Before work, sells mobile? Absolutely not

indicators.note: before says this piece comes first

parts.note: a shop stocks the goods it sells
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A shop sells mobile phones before work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' suggests a phone; it is the adjective, and 'Absolutely not' turns it into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely motionless is the absolute opposite of being mobile.

clue.text: Stealthily moving Liverpool's first away fixture

indicators.note: away means that letter is removed from the longer word

parts.note: flitting, as in a moonlight flit, is moving off quietly to avoid creditors

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A football report: Liverpool's first away fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a football away match; 'away' actually removes L (Liverpool's first) from FLITTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitting is a fixed piece of equipment in a building, such as a light fitting, so it is a fixture.

clue.text: Guitarist (in the style of J. 'endrix) defending troops

parts.note: George Harrison, the Beatles guitarist, gives his initial G

indicators.note: written like J. 'endrix, an initial plus a surname with its H dropped

parts.note: the surname of Beatle George Harrison

explanation.surface: A guitarist mimicking Jimi Hendrix plays to defending soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'J. 'endrix' is Jimi Hendrix written as initial plus H-less surname; George Harrison in that style is G. 'ARRISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of soldiers stationed to defend a town or fort.

clue.text: Quite agree at first

indicators.note: first says the short piece goes before the other

parts.note: at and to are interchangeable in phrases like 'at home' and 'to hand'
accounts tally when they agree

explanation.surface: A short instruction to agree at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite in the sense of completely or entirely, as in 'quite right'.

clue.text: Moving chapter along, author perhaps makes a pile

indicators.note: moving one letter means it is taken out and put back elsewhere in the word
along says the letter shifts further down the word

parts.note: an author is one example of a creator

explanation.surface: An author shifts a chapter around and ends up with a heap of manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' suggests a stack of paper; here it means an atomic pile.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic pile was the early name for a nuclear fission reactor.

clue.text: Funny sort reserves sandwich containing principally cheese

indicators.note: sandwich means the pieces enclose another between them

parts.note: a riot is a hilarious person

indicators.note: principally takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve

explanation.surface: A comedian keeps sandwiches filled mostly with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwich' suggests food but is a verb: the first letter of 'containing', picked by 'principally', is enclosed. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, white Italian whey product is a fresh cheese.

clue.text: Sea area a couple of leagues east of Gibraltar?

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means placed after

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock
L is an abbreviation for league, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A navigational question about waters a few leagues east of Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCKALL is one of the sea areas in the BBC Shipping Forecast, the weather bulletin for waters round the British Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a named zone in the British Shipping Forecast, an islet in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Will's part revoked to make firm money

indicators.note: revoked suggests turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: set means firm or solid
the real is a coin, the currency of Brazil and formerly of Spain

explanation.surface: A legal will is revoked to secure money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is William Shakespeare, so his 'part' is a role in his plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia's brother in Hamlet is a role written by the Bard.

clue.text: Wheedle soft drinks from speaker

indicators.note: from a speaker means the word as it is pronounced, not as written

parts.note: Cokes are cola soft drinks

explanation.surface: Cajoling someone into buying fizzy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle and to coax both mean to persuade with flattery or gentle urging.

clue.text: Performing comic operas without a viewer for the minute

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on or working the letters into a fresh order
without means the letter a is left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Staging comic operas with no audience member watching at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as a moment of time (MIN-it) but is the adjective (my-NEWT) meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens instrument enlarges tiny things, so it is a viewer for what is minute.

clue.text: Wind up English magistrate

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: when the wind changes direction it veers

explanation.surface: Annoy an English justice of the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' reads as tease; 'Wind' is VEER and 'up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval local official or chief officer of a town held a role akin to a magistrate.

clue.text: Could be Man City's second half

indicators.note: second half takes the last four of the eight letters

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in north-west England

explanation.surface: A football remark about Manchester City's second half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man City' is the football club; split it so 'Man' is the Isle of Man and 'City' is Carlisle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is an island, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Is it last of back teeth (molar) needing treatment? Now we're getting somewhere!

indicators.note: teeth needing treatment are to be worked on, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of back

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist asks whether a rear molar needs work, then sounds pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses approval that progress is finally being made, an idiom of improvement.

clue.text: Earth before middle of Bronze Age

indicators.note: before says this letter comes first

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

indicators.note: middle of takes the central pair of letters

explanation.surface: Earth before the Bronze Age.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period of time.

clue.text: Part of organ, the reproductive bit of plant

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A botany description of part of a flower's reproductive organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen is a small part of the plant.

clue.text: Doddering lecturer taking year over geographical alignments

indicators.note: over means the whole assembly is turned round and read backwards
taking means the first pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: doddering means frail and senile with age

explanation.surface: An aged lecturer spends a year on mapping alignments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts Y inside SENILE plus L, giving SENILYEL; 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: These are supposed straight alignments linking ancient sites across the landscape, a folklore of geography.
